page: Amazon Web Services m7a.large is a general-purpose server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz, providing 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs without hyperthreading. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or a GPU, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong single-core capability, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show clear limitations. Multi-core stress-ng performance and write memory bandwidth fall into the average range, while read-only memory bandwidth, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and overall Geekbench multi-core scores are positioned in the bottom 25%. Passmark memory scores and medium-model LLM prompt processing are particularly weak, falling into the bottom 10%, indicating a bottleneck in memory-intensive and heavy parallel processing tasks.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m7a.large offers a balanced entry-level resource profile for workloads that prioritize single-threaded CPU speed over massive memory throughput or parallel execution. Given the dedicated CPU allocation and strong single-core performance, this instance is suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, single-threaded data processing, and small-scale application hosting where local storage is not required.
